title: The Heat Wave That Hit the Pacific Northwest

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the
sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日简报栏目 DealBook

sentences.en: New York Times.
sentences.zh: 的商业与政策报道。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市 DealBook 峰会的现场，采访多位在商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的领袖，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·

sentences.en: Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼等众多嘉宾。

sentences.zh: 你可以直接观看其中一些不加防备、原汁原味的对话实况。

sentences.zh: 我们将对部分采访进行现场直播，任何人都可以于 11 月 18 日

sentences.en: 18th.
sentences.zh: 在 nytimes.com 免费观看。

sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序来观看，并免费获得我们所有新闻报道一个月的访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is A Daily, today.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听今日《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Record-breaking climate extremes are blanketing the United States this summer, from heat to drought to wildfires.
sentences.zh: 今年夏天，从高温、干旱到野火，打破纪录的极端气候正笼罩着整个美国。

sentences.en: Estet Herndon spoke with our colleagues, Sergio Olmos, about the historic heat wave that
sentences.zh: 埃斯特·赫恩顿与我们的同事塞尔吉奥·奥尔莫斯进行了交谈，探讨了席卷

sentences.en: scorched the Pacific Northwest, and to Henry Fountain about how much climate change is to blame.
sentences.zh: 太平洋西北地区的历史性热浪，并与亨利·方丹探讨了气候变化究竟占了多大责任。

sentences.en: It's
sentences.zh: 今天是

sentences.en: Wednesday, July 14th.
sentences.zh: 7月14日，星期三。

sentences.en: Sergio, I feel like Portland has been basically at the center of every national news story recently.
sentences.zh: 塞尔吉奥，我感觉波特兰最近几乎成了每条全国新闻的中心。

sentences.en: Well, we had a pretty extreme year in Portland.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们在波特兰经历了相当极端的一年。

sentences.en: We had COVID shutdowns, 100 days of consecutive protests.
sentences.zh: 我们经历了新冠封锁，以及长达100天的连续抗议活动。

sentences.en: Then we had historic wildfires where the sky just turned red.
sentences.zh: 然后我们遭遇了历史性的野火，天空直接变成了红色。

sentences.en: And then, you know, finally the city's starting to open back up again.
sentences.zh: 再然后，你知道的，这座城市终于开始重新开放了。

sentences.en: COVID restrictions are starting to get lifted.
sentences.zh: 防疫限制开始解除。

sentences.en: People were starting to come out of their houses, go to restaurants, go to bars, and regular life was resuming a little bit.
sentences.zh: 人们开始走出家门，去餐馆，去酒吧，日常生活多少恢复了一些。

sentences.en: And then this massive heat wave just descends on the Pacific
sentences.zh: 然后，这场巨大的热浪就在6月下旬

sentences.en: Northwest in late June.
sentences.zh: 席卷了太平洋西北地区。

sentences.en: The Northwest bracing for record-breaking and potentially life-threatening heat this weekend.
sentences.zh: 西北地区正严阵以待，迎接本周末打破纪录且可能危及生命的高温。

sentences.en: Dozens of records, some of them decades old, are expected to fall.
sentences.zh: 几十个温度记录预计将被打破，其中一些记录已经保持了几十年。

sentences.en: It's Oregon,
sentences.zh: 波及范围包括俄勒冈州、

sentences.en: Washington, and parts of Western Canada.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿州以及加拿大西部的一部分地区。

sentences.en: And it brings this punishing heat.
sentences.zh: 并带来了这种残酷的高温。

sentences.en: Portland hit an all-time record high of 112 earlier today.
sentences.zh: 今天早些时候，波特兰创下了112华氏度的历史最高纪录。

sentences.en: Today in Portland, Oregon, temperatures soared to 114 degrees.
sentences.zh: 今天在俄勒冈州波特兰，气温飙升至114度。

sentences.en: Portland hit 116 degrees Fahrenheit on Monday, making it one of the hottest places in the world.
sentences.zh: 周一波特兰气温达到了116华氏度，使其成为世界上最热的地方之一。

sentences.en: In Portland, we saw temperatures for three days in a row break record after record, and it finally got to 116 degrees.
sentences.zh: 在波特兰，我们看到气温连续三天打破一个又一个纪录，最后达到了116度。

sentences.en: This is some serious heat.
sentences.zh: 这可真是极端的高温。

sentences.en: Average temperatures this time of year, lower and middle 70s.
sentences.zh: 一年中这个时候的平均气温，在70度出头到70度中期。

sentences.en: We're talking about the...
sentences.zh: 我们说的是……

sentences.en: You know, 116 degrees is like 40 degrees above what it should normally be for this time of the year.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，116度比今年这个时候的正常气温高出了大约40度。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And that's nine degrees above the previous record of 107.
sentences.zh: 这比之前107度的纪录高出了整整9度。

sentences.en: Many people there are not used to relying on air conditioning and are needing to seek out cooling centers to stay safe.
sentences.zh: 那里的许多人并不习惯依赖空调，需要寻找避暑中心来确保安全。

sentences.en: And so we see Portland thrown back into the state of emergency, right?
sentences.zh: 所以我们看到波特兰再次陷入紧急状态，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, just like COVID or the protests, the wildfires, everything shuts down, no one's outside.
sentences.zh: 就像新冠疫情、抗议活动或野火一样，一切都关闭了，街上空无一人。

sentences.en: And this time, it's a different catastrophe.
sentences.zh: 而这一次，是一场不同的灾难。

sentences.en: It's heat.
sentences.zh: 是高温。

sentences.en: I know reporters have this weird experience where people are staying in and you run out.
sentences.zh: 我知道记者们都有这种奇怪的经历：人们都呆在家里，而你却要往外跑。

sentences.en: And I know that that is a reporter's shared instinct.
sentences.zh: 我知道这是记者们共同的本能。

sentences.en: But can you describe what it was like over those last couple weeks?
sentences.zh: 但你能描述一下过去这几个星期是什么样的吗？

sentences.en: What has it felt like just physically being in that level of heat?
sentences.zh: 置身于那种程度的高温中，身体上的感觉究竟是怎样的？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It felt like a walk out of the door and the heat wave hits you.
sentences.zh: 感觉就像是一出门，热浪就扑面而来。

sentences.en: It's like, oh, okay.
sentences.zh: 那种感觉就是，哦，好吧。

sentences.en: Feels like Vegas, right?
sentences.zh: 感觉就像在拉斯维加斯，对吧？

sentences.en: But I'm in Portland.
sentences.zh: 但我身处波特兰。

sentences.en: This is the Pacific Northwest, right?
sentences.zh: 这里可是太平洋西北地区，对吧？

sentences.en: Where it's raining a lot of the time.
sentences.zh: 那里大部分时间都在下雨。

sentences.en: It's cool.
sentences.zh: 天气很凉爽。

sentences.en: It's not a place you think of to buy an AC.
sentences.zh: 这不是一个你会想到去买空调的地方。

sentences.en: It never gets that hot.
sentences.zh: 这里从没这么热过。

sentences.en: We're not used to this.
sentences.zh: 我们对此很不习惯。

sentences.en: The 116 degree weather is something that, like, the health officer here for the county explained it, that bodies acclimate to heat, but it takes time.
sentences.zh: 正如该县卫生官员所解释的那样，116度的天气，人体对热是会适应的，但这需要时间。

sentences.en: You can't just acclimate one day to the next, one weekend to the next.
sentences.zh: 你不可能从一天到第二天、从一个周末到下一个周末就突然适应。

sentences.en: And so, yeah, we're not acclimated to that.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我们根本没有适应这种天气。

sentences.en: And our infrastructure is not built for it.
sentences.zh: 我们的基础设施也不是为此建造的。

sentences.en: For instance, I was driving around and a few, just a few blocks from my house.
sentences.zh: 例如，我当时开车四处转转，就在离我家仅几条街的地方。

sentences.en: In the middle of the road, the pavement just buckled.
sentences.zh: 路面竟然直接拱起来了。

sentences.en: It cracked and it rose up.
sentences.zh: 它裂开并向上凸起。

sentences.en: And the city said it was heat related.
sentences.zh: 市政府表示这与高温有关。

sentences.en: I don't know anything about pavement instead, but I assume it wasn't.
sentences.zh: 我对路面一窍不通，但我想确实是的。

sentences.en: I've never seen it buckle.
sentences.zh: 我从来没见过路面拱起过。

sentences.en: So you've already got me shocked.
sentences.zh: 所以你已经把我惊到了。

sentences.en: Public transportation here, right?
sentences.zh: 这里的公共交通也是，对吧？

sentences.en: So the city ahead of time was like, hey, it's public transportation is going to be free this weekend.
sentences.zh: 因此，市政府提前宣布：嘿，这周末的公共交通将免费。

sentences.en: If you need to get to the cooling center or anything, just get on there.
sentences.zh: 如果你需要去避暑中心或其他地方，直接上车就行。

sentences.en: Don't worry about paying for it.
sentences.zh: 不用担心付车费。

sentences.en: But as soon as the heat hit, the streetcars and the trains, they stopped them because the overhead wires for the light rail system were being strained.
sentences.zh: 但高温一旦袭来，有轨电车和火车就停运了，因为轻轨系统的架空电线承受了巨大的压力。

sentences.en: They were only designed to work in temperatures of up to 110 degrees.
sentences.zh: 它们原本的设计只能在高达110度的温度下运行。

sentences.en: And the streetcars, the cables that power them were actually melting.
sentences.zh: 而有轨电车的供电电缆实际上已经开始融化了。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So they, the city of Portland paused all trains, all streetcars at the time they needed them the most, right?
sentences.zh: 所以波特兰市政府在最需要它们的时刻，暂停了所有的火车和有轨电车，对吧？

sentences.en: So it was harder for some people just to get to the cooling centers.
sentences.zh: 因此，有些人想要前往避暑中心变得更加困难了。

sentences.en: And there's a socioeconomic aspect to all of this.
sentences.zh: 这一切背后还存在着社会经济层面的问题。

sentences.en: There's a professor at Portland State
sentences.zh: 波特兰州立大学

sentences.en: University named Vivek Shandis, and he studies climate adaptation.
sentences.zh: 有一位教授名叫维韦克·尚迪斯（Vivek Shandas），他专门研究气候适应问题。

sentences.en: And during the heat wave, he went around Portland with a thermometer.
sentences.zh: 在热浪期间，他拿着一支温度计在波特兰四处走动。

sentences.en: It's not the kind you buy at the store.
sentences.zh: 这不是你在商店里买的那种。

sentences.en: It's a scientific grade thermometer.
sentences.zh: 这是科学级的温度计。

sentences.en: And he took measurements of different parts of Portland.
sentences.zh: 他对波特兰的不同区域进行了测量。

sentences.en: And he found that the wealthiest parts of Portland were in some cases, 98, 99 degrees, right?
sentences.zh: 他发现波特兰最富裕的地区，在某些情况下气温是98度、99度，对吧？

sentences.en: And then he went to the working class parts of Portland, parts of Portland where the highest concentration of people of color historically have been disinvested.
sentences.zh: 然后他去了波特兰的工人阶级区，也就是历史上集中了大量有色人种、且长期缺乏投资的波特兰地区。

sentences.en: So not a lot of sidewalks, not a lot of tree covers, a lot of exposed to sun and a lot of concrete that just absorbs the sun's radiation.
sentences.zh: 那里没有多少人行道，没有多少树荫，大量暴露在阳光下，还有很多会吸收太阳辐射的混凝土。

sentences.en: He found a reading of
sentences.zh: 他测得的读数

sentences.en: 121 degrees in the poorest neighborhoods in Portland.
sentences.zh: 在波特兰最贫穷的街区达到了121度。

sentences.en: And so if you look at that and look at the big picture here, the county released a map of where people died in the city.
sentences.zh: 如果你看看这些，再看看这里的全貌，就会发现该县发布了一张市内人员死亡地点的地图。

sentences.en: And in the poorest zip codes, the highest number of deaths occurred.
sentences.zh: 在最贫困的邮政编码区域，死亡人数最多。

sentences.en: And in the wealthiest zip codes, we had the lowest number of deaths occur.
sentences.zh: 而在最富裕的邮政编码区域，死亡人数最少。

sentences.en: And what do we know about the people who died?
sentences.zh: 我们对死者有什么了解？

sentences.en: Who are they?
sentences.zh: 他们都是些什么人？

sentences.en: Right now, at least 193 people have died across Oregon and Washington related to the heat.
sentences.zh: 目前，俄勒冈州和华盛顿州已有至少 193 人因高温死亡。

sentences.en: What we know is that many of the people who died were elderly, living alone, without air conditioning.
sentences.zh: 我们所知道的是，许多死者都是独居的老人，家中没有空调。

sentences.en: Others were homeless, and others had underlying health conditions.
sentences.zh: 其他人则是无家可归者，还有一些人本身就有潜在的健康问题。

sentences.en: For example, there's a story of an 84-year-old woman in Washington state, Dorothy Galliano, who was found dead in her home.
sentences.zh: 例如，华盛顿州有一位84岁的老妇人多萝西·加利亚诺（Dorothy Galliano），她被发现死在家中。

sentences.en: She lived alone and had no air conditioning.
sentences.zh: 她独居且没有安装空调。

sentences.en: A friend said that she was found with the window cracked open and the TV on.
sentences.zh: 一位朋友说，被发现时窗户开着一条缝，电视还开着。

sentences.en: And she just imagined that Dorothy was watching TV, dozed off, and just didn't wake up.
sentences.zh: 她想象着多萝西当时在看电视，打了个盹，然后就再也没有醒来。

sentences.en: Another woman, Deborah Moore, was found collapsed on the sidewalk just a few steps from a house she was visiting.
sentences.zh: 另一位名叫黛博拉·穆尔（Deborah Moore）的妇女，被发现倒在人行道上，距离她正在拜访的一栋房子只有几步之遥。

sentences.en: And the police said that she had serious underlying health issues.
sentences.zh: 警方表示，她有着严重的潜在健康问题。

sentences.en: You have the story of a houseless man, Joseph Wade Davis, who's 64.
sentences.zh: 还有64岁的无家可归男子约瑟夫·韦德·戴维斯（Joseph Wade Davis）的故事。

sentences.en: And he had just this tent on the side of the road with PVC pipe and tarp.
sentences.zh: 他就在路边搭了一个用PVC管和防水布搭成的帐篷。

sentences.en: And he was just discovered dead at 10 a.m.
sentences.zh: 结果他在早上10点被发现已经死亡。

sentences.en: So it's a mix of people, obviously the most vulnerable, elderly, who were living alone without AC, homeless folks.
sentences.zh: 所以死者背景各异，显然最脆弱的是独居且无空调的老人，以及无家可归的人。

sentences.en: These are, you know, the highest number.
sentences.zh: 这些人占了，你知道的，最高的人数比例。

sentences.en: But there are other people, you know, healthy adults who also died.
sentences.zh: 但也有其他人，比如健康的成年人也不幸身亡。

sentences.en: And some of them died at work.
sentences.zh: 其中有些人是在工作中死去的。

sentences.en: Sebastian Francisco Perez, he was the first reported workplace fatality related to the heat.
sentences.zh: 塞巴斯蒂安·弗朗西斯科·佩雷斯（Sebastian Francisco Perez），他是第一起被报道的与高温相关的工作场所死亡病例。
zh_words: 塞巴斯蒂安·弗朗西斯科·佩雷斯

sentences.en: And he died in the Willamette Valley, where he lived and worked.
sentences.zh: 他在自己生活和工作的威拉米特谷去世了。

sentences.en: And so I went there to learn more about them.
sentences.zh: 所以我去那里了解更多关于他们的信息。

sentences.en: And it's like a farmland community there where they grow a lot of like fruit, trees, and kind of the breadbasket of Oregon.
sentences.zh: 那里就像是一个农田社区，种植大量的水果、树木之类的作物，可以说是俄勒冈州的粮仓。

sentences.en: And I eventually tracked down his brother-in-law and his nephew.
sentences.zh: 我最终找到了他的连襟和侄子。

sentences.en: And they're working in the field when I find them.
sentences.zh: 我找到他们时，他们正在地里干活。

sentences.en: And he tells me about Sebastian Francisco
sentences.zh: 他向我讲述了塞巴斯蒂安·弗朗西斯科
zh_words: 塞巴斯蒂安·弗朗西斯科

sentences.en: Perez.
sentences.zh: 佩雷斯的事迹。

sentences.en: He came from Guatemala three months ago.
sentences.zh: 他三个月前刚从危地马拉来到这里。

sentences.en: He wanted to have children, but he couldn't afford it in Guatemala.
sentences.zh: 他想要孩子，但在危地马拉根本养不起。

sentences.en: Lived just very austere conditions.
sentences.zh: 过着非常简朴的生活。

sentences.en: They grew their food.
sentences.zh: 他们自己种粮食度日。

sentences.en: They didn't have any wages.
sentences.zh: 没有任何薪水。

sentences.en: Came here to try to, you know, get some money to start a family.
sentences.zh: 来到这里是为了，你知道的，攒点钱组建家庭。

sentences.en: And he owed a coyote.
sentences.zh: 而且他还欠着蛇头一笔钱。

sentences.en: These are the people that help immigrants cross illegally.
sentences.zh: 也就是帮助移民偷渡的人。

sentences.en: He'd owed him $8,000 for the crossing, five up front, three after.
sentences.zh: 他欠了8000美元的偷渡费，首付5000，事后付3000。

sentences.en: And so he was desperate to work.
sentences.zh: 因此他极度渴望工作。

sentences.en: And, you know, that Saturday when it was extraordinarily hot, and a lot of farm workers who could take the day off took it.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，那个异常炎热的周六，许多可以请假的农场工人都没有去上班。

sentences.en: He asked to work.
sentences.zh: 而他却要求工作。

sentences.en: He was told by a relative, like, don't do it.
sentences.zh: 一位亲戚曾对他说，别去了。

sentences.en: It's too hot.
sentences.zh: 天气太热了。

sentences.en: And he said, no, please, I need the money.
sentences.zh: 他说，不，求你了，我需要钱。

sentences.en: That Saturday, he was moving irrigation lines in a field of trees.
sentences.zh: 那个星期六，他正在一片树林里移动灌溉水管。

sentences.en: And his co-workers, other laborers, found him collapsed among the trees.
sentences.zh: 他的同事和其他劳工发现他倒在了树丛中。

sentences.en: And they called 911.
sentences.zh: 他们拨打了911。

sentences.en: But they couldn't tell the operator where he was exactly.
sentences.zh: 但他们无法准确告诉接线员他所在的位置。

sentences.en: You know, a lot of the laborers, a lot of the immigrants, you know, they work from farm to farm and they get brought in together and they don't necessarily know where
sentences.zh: 你知道的，很多劳工，很多移民，他们一个农场接一个农场地打工，被一起带到各个地方，并不一定

sentences.en: they are all the time.
sentences.zh: 时时刻刻都知道自己在哪。

sentences.en: So they called his nephew and they said, hey, he's collapsed on the ground.
sentences.zh: 于是他们给他的侄子打电话说，嘿，他倒在地上吐了。

sentences.en: We don't know what to do.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道该怎么办。

sentences.en: He tells him, take him to the shade.
sentences.zh: 侄子告诉他们：把他弄到阴凉处去。

sentences.en: I'm on my way.
sentences.zh: 我正在赶过去。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, couldn't resuscitate him.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，没能救活他。

sentences.en: He died that day.
sentences.zh: 他那天去世了。

sentences.en: So this heat wave was kind of an opening salvo to what's going to be a catastrophic season.
sentences.zh: 所以这次热浪可以说是即将到来的灾难性季节的开端。

sentences.en: The West is currently in the midst of historic drought.
sentences.zh: 西部目前正处于历史性的干旱之中。

sentences.en: Another heat wave is already sweeping across California in the SouthweSt. And fire season has already begun here in Oregon.
sentences.zh: 另一场热浪已经席卷加利福尼亚和西南部。俄勒冈州的火灾季节也已经在这里开始了。

sentences.en: And this is this is unprecedented, right?
sentences.zh: 这真是前所未有，对吧？

sentences.en: This is the earliest in the year that I've covered a wildfire season.
sentences.zh: 这是我历年来报道过的最早的一次野火季。

sentences.en: There's a fire right now burning in Oregon.
sentences.zh: 俄勒冈州现在正燃起大火。

sentences.en: It's uncontained.
sentences.zh: 火势尚未得到控制。

sentences.en: It's already burned
sentences.zh: 截至周一，

sentences.en: 150,000 acres as of Monday.
sentences.zh: 已经烧毁了15万英亩土地。

sentences.en: And nobody expected the season to begin this early or already have been this destructive.
sentences.zh: 没有人预料到这个季节会开始得这么早，而且已经具有如此大的破坏力。

sentences.en: So from one climate disaster to the next.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一场接一场的气候灾难。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Thank you, Sergio.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，塞尔吉奥。

sentences.en: Thank you, you said, we'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，你说的对，我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app unlocked.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序已解锁。

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month for free without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你不用输入信用卡就能免费体验《时报》一个月呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用里的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间可以突破付费墙，看看《时报》订户每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是《纽约时报》的订户，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Okay, Henry, I've been speaking with our colleague who has been reporting on the heat waves out in the WeSt. There was the record-breaking one that happened in
sentences.zh: 好的，亨利，我一直在与我们一直在报道西部热浪的同事交谈。有一场创纪录的热浪发生在

sentences.en: June in the Pacific Northwest and another that's underway in California.
sentences.zh: 6月的美国太平洋西北地区，另一场正在加利福尼亚州发生。

sentences.en: The question that's running in the back of my head is, how much of what we're seeing is related to climate change?
sentences.zh: 我脑子里一直闪现的一个问题是，我们所看到的现象有多少与气候变化有关？

sentences.en: Well, you know, that's the question that journalists and others always ask after a heat wave or other kind of extreme weather event.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，这是记者和其他人在热浪或其他极端天气事件发生后总是会问的问题。

sentences.en: And it's really a central question.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一个核心问题。

sentences.en: So right after the late June heat wave in the Pacific Northwest, in fact, there was actually a group of scientists trying to figure that very question out.
sentences.zh: 因此，就在6月下旬太平洋西北地区热浪发生后不久，实际上有一群科学家试图弄清楚这个问题。

sentences.en: Good morning.
sentences.zh: 早上好。

sentences.en: Good afternoon.
sentences.zh: 下午好。

sentences.en: Thank you very much for joining.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你们的加入。

sentences.en: This group is called World Weather Attribution, and they held a press conference on Zoom announcing their findings.
sentences.zh: 这个组织被称为“世界天气归因”，他们在Zoom上举行了一场新闻发布会，宣布了他们的研究结果。

sentences.en: It was led by Gerd Jan van Oldenburg and Frederica Otto.
sentences.zh: 该研究由赫尔特·扬·范·奥尔登伯格和弗雷德里卡·奥托领导。
zh_words: 赫尔特·扬·范·奥尔登伯格

sentences.en: In our study, we focus on the hottest day of the year, which is what broke the records and what you will have heard in the news.
sentences.zh: 在我们的研究中，我们关注的是一年中最热的一天，正是这一天打破了纪录，也就是你在新闻中听到的那样。

sentences.en: So the question immediately arrives, what is the role of climate change in this event?
sentences.zh: 所以紧接着出现的问题是，气候变化在这场事件中起到了什么作用？

sentences.en: They try to figure out a link, if it exists, between the world that's warming and these extreme events, like this really, really bad heat wave.
sentences.zh: 他们试图找出变暖的世界与这些极端事件（比如这场非常非常严重的热浪）之间是否存在某种联系。

sentences.en: And they try to do it really quickly.
sentences.zh: 而且他们试图以非常快的速度完成这项工作。

sentences.en: We have done this study within a week, and everyone worked nights and weekends.
sentences.zh: 我们在不到一周的时间里完成了这项研究，所有人都通宵达旦、加班加点。

sentences.en: They think that getting it out when it's still fresh in people's minds would help people understand the problem.
sentences.zh: 他们认为，在人们记忆犹新的时候将其公之于众，将有助于人们理解这个问题。

sentences.en: And how exactly do they do that analysis?
sentences.zh: 他们究竟是如何进行这种分析的？

sentences.en: How do they measure the impact of climate change when it comes to a single event?
sentences.zh: 在涉及单一事件时，他们如何衡量气候变化的影响？

sentences.en: They use a lot of computers, basically, that run models of the world.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他们使用了大量运行世界模型的计算机。

sentences.en: They simulate the world.
sentences.zh: 他们模拟这个世界。

sentences.en: And they run some models with the world as it is today, which is, it's warmed about two degrees Fahrenheit because we've poured all the CO2 into the atmosphere.
sentences.zh: 他们运行了一些以当今世界为基准的模型，这个世界已经变暖了大约华氏两度，因为我们向大气中排放了所有的二氧化碳。

sentences.en: They also run models of a world that exists or would exist if we hadn't pumped all that CO2 in the atmosphere.
sentences.zh: 他们还模拟了一个如果没有将所有这些二氧化碳排放到大气中而存在或将会存在的世界的模型。

sentences.en: In other words, a world without warming.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，这是一个没有变暖的世界。

sentences.en: And then they compare the two results.
sentences.zh: 然后他们比较这两个结果。

sentences.en: So, for instance, if a heat wave like this had a 1 in 100 chance of occurring in a given year in a
sentences.zh: 因此，举例来说，如果在

sentences.en: world that hadn't warmed, and in a world that warmed, it has a 1 in 10 chance of happening in a given year, then you know that climate change had an impact.
sentences.zh: 一个没有变暖的世界里，像这样的一次热浪在特定年份发生的几率是百分之一；而在一个变暖的世界里，它在特定年份发生的几率是十分之一，那么你就知道气候变化产生了影响。

sentences.en: So when these scientists ran this model, what did they find?
sentences.zh: 那么，当这些科学家运行这个模型时，他们发现了什么？

sentences.en: Well, what you've got to understand about this heat wave, it was really off the charts.
sentences.zh: 嗯，关于这场热浪，你必须明白的是，它真的是前所未有的。

sentences.en: It was extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 这太非同寻常了。

sentences.en: We've never seen a jump in record temperature like the one in this heat wave, as far as I can remember.
sentences.zh: 就我的记忆所及，我们从未见过像这次热浪这样温度纪录飙升的情况。

sentences.en: And when they ran the analysis, the results were clear.
sentences.zh: 当他们进行分析时，结果非常清晰。

sentences.en: There's absolutely no doubt that that climate change played a key role here.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，气候变化在其中起到了关键作用。

sentences.en: This extreme heat wave in this place would have been impossible before we started warming the world.
sentences.zh: 在我们开始让世界变暖之前，这个地方发生的这场极端热浪是不可能发生的。

sentences.en: It means that without the additional greenhouse gases in the atmosphere, such an event just does never occur.
sentences.zh: 这意味着如果没有大气中额外的温室气体，这样的事件是绝不会发生的。

sentences.en: Or if it occurs, it occurs once in a million times, which is the statistical equivalent of never.
sentences.zh: 或者如果它发生了，那也是百万分之一的几率，这在统计学上等同于永不发生。

sentences.en: So it was still a rare event, but 100 years ago, it was an impossible event.
sentences.zh: 所以这仍然是一个罕见的事件，但在100年前，这是一个不可能发生的事件。

sentences.en: And that's because the world is warmed.
sentences.zh: 这就是因为世界变暖了。

sentences.en: So heat waves are increasing in likelihood by orders of magnitude more than any other type of extreme event.
sentences.zh: 因此，热浪发生的可能性比任何其他类型的极端天气事件都要高出好几个数量级。

sentences.en: And what these researchers have also found is that heat waves are more affected by climate change than any other extreme weather.
sentences.zh: 这些研究人员还发现，与其他任何极端天气相比，热浪受气候变化的影响更大。

sentences.en: So for any other type of extreme event, we do see
sentences.zh: 因此，对于任何其他类型的极端事件，我们确实会看到

sentences.en: extreme rainfall or droughts.
sentences.zh: 极端的降雨或干旱。

sentences.en: We do see an increase maybe by a factor of four.
sentences.zh: 我们确实看到可能性增加了大约四倍。

sentences.en: But for heat waves, we see orders of magnitude.
sentences.zh: 但对于热浪，我们看到的是数量级的增加。

sentences.en: So this event was made at least 150 times more likely.
sentences.zh: 因此，这次事件发生的可能性至少增加了150倍。

sentences.en: And she said that heat waves, more than any other type of climate-related natural disaster, are not only more likely, but they also tend to kill more people.
sentences.zh: 她表示，与其他任何类型的气候相关自然灾害相比，热浪不仅更有可能发生，而且往往会夺走更多人的生命。

sentences.en: And yeah, and I think this is really, heat waves is how climate change kills us today.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这确实是，热浪正是气候变化如今夺走我们生命的方式。

sentences.en: I think this is this is how climate change manifests most strongly.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是气候变化表现得最强烈的方式。

sentences.en: Just think about it.
sentences.zh: 仔细想想。

sentences.en: You know, a flood might affect a relatively small region, an area near a river or whatever, but a heat wave can cover a huge amount of area.
sentences.zh: 你知道，洪水可能会影响相对较小的区域，比如河流附近或其他地方的区域，但热浪可以覆盖巨大的面积。

sentences.en: In this Pacific Northwest heat wave that ended in the end of June, everybody in Oregon, everybody in the state of Washington, and most of
sentences.zh: 在6月底结束的太平洋西北地区热浪中，俄勒冈州的每个人、华盛顿州的每个人，以及

sentences.en: the people in British Columbia were affected.
sentences.zh: 不列颠哥伦比亚省的大多数人

sentences.en: So I think the researchers estimated that that was something like 9 million people.
sentences.zh: 都受到了影响。因此，研究人员估计，这大约影响了900万人。

sentences.en: And that's a really a lot of potential victims of extreme heat.
sentences.zh: 这真的是一个极其庞大的极端高温潜在受害者群体。

sentences.en: And so all of this has these scientists concerned.
sentences.zh: 因此，所有这一切都让这些科学家感到担忧。

sentences.en: We feel that we do not understand heat waves as well as we thought we did.
sentences.zh: 我们觉得自己对热浪的了解并没有想象中那么深刻。

sentences.en: You know, I've covered a bunch of these attribution studies, and I've talked to a lot of scientists about them.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我报道过一系列这样的归因研究，我也和很多科学家谈过这些研究。

sentences.en: And normally, it's pretty straightforward.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，情况相当简单明了。

sentences.en: But there's one thing Dr.
sentences.zh: 但范·奥尔登伯格博士说的有一句话

sentences.en: van Oldenborg said that really struck me.
sentences.zh: 真的让我印象深刻。

sentences.en: And I, frankly, I kind of found it alarming.
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，我觉得这有点令人担忧。

sentences.en: I think most of us, or all of us, have just dialed down our certainty of how heat waves behave.
sentences.zh: 我想我们大多数人，或者我们所有人，都降低了对热浪行为方式的确定性。

sentences.en: We are much less certain about how the climate affects heat waves than we were two weeks ago.
sentences.zh: 我们对气候如何影响热浪的确定性远不如两周前了。

sentences.en: You know, essentially he said, like, you know, after this heat wave, it was so unusual, so extreme.
sentences.zh: 从本质上讲，他说，你知道，在经历这场热浪之后，它是如此的不寻常，如此极端。

sentences.en: We're not sure we really understand heat waves anymore.
sentences.zh: 我们不确定自己是否真的还了解热浪。

sentences.en: Like, it's really kind of jolted us, you know, in our certainty of the way heat waves behave.
sentences.zh: 这确实让我们对热浪行为方式的确定性受到了震撼。

sentences.en: Henry, it sounds like what you're saying is what really surprised you is the fact that the
sentences.zh: 亨利，听起来你的意思是，真正让你感到惊讶的事实是

sentences.en: scientists themselves were surprised, and that they were saying the heat wave that was just
sentences.zh: 科学家们自己也感到惊讶，并且他们说刚刚经历的

sentences.en: experienced in the Northwest may have actually changed their understanding of how these operate.
sentences.zh: 西北地区热浪实际上可能改变了他们对这些现象运作机制的理解。

sentences.en: What exactly are we saying, though?
sentences.zh: 不过，我们究竟在说什么呢？

sentences.en: How is this heat wave possibly different than ones that we have seen previously?
sentences.zh: 这场热浪怎么可能与我们以前见过的热浪有所不同？

sentences.en: So what we'd expect with a kind of quote-unquote normal heat wave is that as the
sentences.zh: 因此，对于所谓“正常”的热浪，我们的预期是，随着

sentences.en: average baseline temperature goes up, you'd expect the hottest record-breaking temperatures to go up at about the same rate, more or less.
sentences.zh: 平均基准温度上升，你会预期打破纪录的最高温度也会以大致相同的速率上升，大体如此。

sentences.en: But with this heat wave in the Pacific Northwest, the highest temperatures broke the record not by a couple of degrees, but by as many as nine degrees.
sentences.zh: 但对于太平洋西北地区的这场热浪，最高气温打破纪录的幅度不是几度，而是高达九度。

sentences.en: So the scientists are trying to figure out what's going on here, and they say there's really only two possibilities.
sentences.zh: 因此，科学家们正试图弄清楚这里发生了什么，他们表示实际上只有两种可能。

sentences.en: The first one is the obvious one, is that it was just a really, really rare event, and this region was unlucky.
sentences.zh: 第一种是显而易见的，即这只是一次非常非常罕见的事件，而这个地区运气不好。

sentences.en: Maybe it's just this confluence of bad luck, as they put it.
sentences.zh: 也许这只是他们所说的厄运的巧合。

sentences.en: I mean, the Earth is a really huge place, and weird things happen, or very improbable happen somewhere on Earth on a fairly regular basis.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，地球是一个非常巨大的地方，奇怪的事情会发生，或者极不可能发生的事情在地球上的某个地方以相当规律的频率发生。

sentences.en: Pacific Northwest had a heat wave that was compounded by the drought that's been going on in the West, and the jet's dream was acting funny, or whatever.
sentences.zh: 太平洋西北地区遭遇的热浪与西部正在发生的干旱叠加在一起，而且急流的表现有些异常，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And maybe that's the case, and in that case, maybe it's not such a concern.
sentences.zh: 也许情况就是这样，如果是这样的话，也许就没那么令人担忧了。

sentences.en: The second possibility is that we could be past a threshold that made these kind of heat wave suddenly much more likely.
sentences.zh: 第二种可能性是，我们可能已经越过了一个阈值，使得这类热浪突然变得更有可能发生。

sentences.en: But if it's some other mechanism, some other threshold idea, that's a concern.
sentences.zh: 但如果涉及其他机制、其他阈值的概念，那就令人担忧了。

sentences.en: Maybe, you know, this one-time event now becomes once every five years, or 10 years, or once a year, or whatever.
sentences.zh: 也许，你知道，这种原本一次性的事件现在变成每五年、每十年或每年发生一次，诸如此类。

sentences.en: So that's the fundamental issue they're trying to figure out.
sentences.zh: 所以这是他们试图弄清楚的根本问题。

sentences.en: More and more, I think this is like, this heat wave is like a big deal.
sentences.zh: 越来越多的情况是，我认为这场热浪就像是一件大事。

sentences.en: It's like a seminal event, really.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一个具有开创性的事件。

sentences.en: Kind of like, you know, a big volcanic eruption or something.
sentences.zh: 有点像，你知道，一次大型火山爆发之类的。

sentences.en: And it's going to be studied for a long time, because it was so unusual.
sentences.zh: 它将被研究很长一段时间，因为它是如此的不寻常。

sentences.en: And they've got to figure out why.
sentences.zh: 他们必须弄清楚原因。

sentences.en: So what's most alarming about their findings is that it could mean that we have hit a sort of tipping point.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们的发现中最令人担忧的是，这可能意味着我们已经触及了一种临界点。

sentences.en: It's not necessarily that we've hit a tipping point.
sentences.zh: 这并不一定意味着我们已经触及了临界点。

sentences.en: But the thing that really stuns a lot of climate scientists, and it certainly stuns a lot of people, is how fast things are happening, right?
sentences.zh: 但真正让许多气候科学家以及许多人感到震惊的是，事情发生的速度是如此之快，对吧？

sentences.en: I'm guilty of this, too.
sentences.zh: 我也有同感。

sentences.en: I've been, you know, writing about climate change for a while, and it was always like, yeah, you know, the big impacts are going to be like in the middle of the century.
sentences.zh: 我一直在，你知道，撰写关于气候变迁的文章有一段时间了，情况总是这样：哦，你知道，巨大的影响将在本世纪中叶显现。

sentences.en: Well, you know, the big impacts are starting now.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你知道，巨大的影响现在已经开始了。

sentences.en: And it's obvious now that the impacts are hitting us.
sentences.zh: 现在很明显，这些影响正在冲击我们。

sentences.en: But it seems like they're sort of accelerating.
sentences.zh: 但它们似乎正在加速。

sentences.en: So whether we've passed a tipping point or not, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 所以我们是否已经越过了临界点，我不知道。

sentences.en: But we're in a bad state right now where bad climate events are happening.
sentences.zh: 但我们目前处于一种糟糕的境地，糟糕的气候事件正在发生。

sentences.en: And what we thought would happen in the future is happening now.
sentences.zh: 我们原以为将来才会发生的事情现在正在发生。

sentences.en: This makes me think back to the beginning of our conversation, when you were talking about
sentences.zh: 这让我想起了我们对话的开头，当时你正在谈论

sentences.en: all of those scientists who are rushing to get information out to the public after each of these extreme weather events.
sentences.zh: 所有那些在每次极端天气事件发生后急于向公众发布信息的科学家。

sentences.en: There seems to be an optimism at the core of that effort, a belief that with a little more information, with a little more knowledge, that policymakers
sentences.zh: 这种努力的核心似乎蕴含着一种乐观主义，一种坚信只要有更多的一点信息，只要有更多的一点知识，决策者

sentences.en: and the public will care more about this issue, will push people to do something.
sentences.zh: 和公众就会更加关心这个问题，从而推动人们采取行动。

sentences.en: But I guess I'm wondering, is that true?
sentences.zh: 但我想我在想，这是真的吗？

sentences.en: Is this really a problem of lack of information?
sentences.zh: 这真的是一个缺乏信息的问题吗？

sentences.en: Well, a couple of things.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有几点。

sentences.en: You know, scientists are scientists, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道，科学家就是科学家，对吧？

sentences.en: They're like men and women who believe in empirical thought and experimentation and getting data and analyzing it and figuring out what's going on and explaining it.
sentences.zh: 他们就像是相信经验主义思想、实验、获取数据、分析数据、弄清楚发生了什么并进行解释的男女。

sentences.en: If they're optimistic, they think they're going to do what they can do, which is explain the world the way it is, the physical world, the warming world to people.
sentences.zh: 如果他们是乐观的，他们认为自己会做力所能及的事情，那就是向人们解释世界的现状、物理世界以及变暖的世界。

sentences.en: And then there are some scientists who then take that and use it to, you know, go out and directly influence the policymakers, like they go lobby Congress or whatever.
sentences.zh: 然后有一些科学家会将其拿来并用于，你知道的，直接去影响决策者，比如他们去游说国会什么的。

sentences.en: But there's a lot who just think, I'm going to do my job.
sentences.zh: 但也有很多人只是想：我要做好我自己的工作。

sentences.en: And then it's up to the public and the public's elected officials to do their job and deal with it.
sentences.zh: 然后就轮到公众和公众选出的官员来做好他们的工作并应对这些问题了。

sentences.en: And, you know, I think you've seen some of that.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我想你已经看到了其中的一些表现。

sentences.en: Scientists have gotten better about explaining what's going on more quickly.
sentences.zh: 科学家们在更快地解释正在发生的事情方面已经做得更好了。

sentences.en: And this whole attribution study by this group, I mean, that's their goal.
sentences.zh: 这个群体进行的整个归因研究，我的意思是，这就是他们的目标。

sentences.en: But what's really going to change people's minds is the more they're personally affected by things like heat waves or floods or droughts, particularly if they
sentences.zh: 但真正能改变人们想法的是他们个人越来越多地受到热浪、洪水或干旱等事件的影响，特别是如果这些事件

sentences.en: keep happening or if, God forbid, they lose a loved one to a flood or to a heat wave.
sentences.zh: 不断发生，或者天哪，如果他们因洪水或热浪失去了一位挚爱的人。

sentences.en: I guess the glass half full read is that as these things like heat waves become more tangible in people's lives, then something will be done.
sentences.zh: 我想乐观看待的话就是，随着热浪这些事情在人们的生活中变得更加切实可感，人们就会采取行动。

sentences.en: But that same view also means that a lot of bad things are going to happen to people before they really come to know the bad effects of climate change.
sentences.zh: 但同样的观点也意味着，在人们真正认识到气候变化的恶劣影响之前，许多糟糕的事情将会降临到他们头上。

sentences.en: And we know that the people who are most likely to experience those negative effects are the people
sentences.zh: 我们知道，最有可能经历这些负面影响的人

sentences.en: who are most vulnerable in our communities, the people who are most unheard, the people who have the least amount of political power to do something about it.
sentences.zh: 是我们社区中最脆弱的人、最不被倾听的人、在采取行动方面政治权力最小的人。

sentences.en: You know, sadly, I think that's really true.
sentences.zh: 你知道，可悲的是，我认为这千真万确。

sentences.en: The poorest and most disadvantaged people in society tend to suffer the most from all kinds of climate-related disasters.
sentences.zh: 社会中最贫困和最弱势的人往往承受着来自各种气候相关灾害的最严重的打击。

sentences.en: And heat waves are really no exception.
sentences.zh: 而热浪也确实不例外。

sentences.en: And what we've learned is that as the world continues to warm, heat waves are going to continue to increase in frequency and get hotter.
sentences.zh: 我们了解到的是，随着世界持续变暖，热浪的发生频率将继续增加，温度也会变得更高。

sentences.en: And we may even see more events like this one in the Pacific Northwest with really off-the-charts extreme heat.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至可能会看到更多像太平洋西北地区那样的极端高温事件，其温度简直突破天际。

sentences.en: And that doesn't bode well for all of society, but it's especially bad news for the poorest and disadvantaged among us.
sentences.zh: 这不仅对整个社会是个不祥之兆，对我们当中最贫困和弱势的群体来说，更是个极其糟糕的消息。

sentences.en: Thank you, Henry, for your time.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，亨利，百忙之中接受采访。

sentences.en: Well, thanks.
sentences.zh: 好的，谢谢。

sentences.en: Nice talking to you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴和你聊天。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他内容。

sentences.en: So hear me clearly.
sentences.zh: 所以请听清楚我的话。

sentences.en: There's an unfolding assault taking place in America today, an attempt to suppress and subvert the right to vote in fair and free elections, an assault on democracy,
sentences.zh: 今天在美利坚正在上演一场持续的攻击，有人企图压制和颠覆在公正自由选举中的投票权，这是对民主的攻击，

sentences.en: an assault on liberty, an assault on who we are, who we are as Americans.
sentences.zh: 对自由的攻击，对我们是谁、我们作为美国人是谁的攻击。

sentences.en: In a speech delivered on Tuesday in Philadelphia, President Biden issued his most forceful denunciation
sentences.zh: 周二在费城发表的一场演讲中，拜登总统发表了他迄今为止最强烈的谴责，

sentences.en: to date of Republican efforts to restrict voting in states across the country and to cast doubt on the legitimacy of his victory.
sentences.zh: 针对的是全国各州共和党人限制投票的企图，以及质疑他胜选合法性的做法。

sentences.en: Bullies and merchants of fear, peddlers of lies, are threatening the very foundation of our country.
sentences.zh: 恃强凌弱者、贩卖恐惧者和散布谎言者，正在威胁我们国家的最根本基石。

sentences.en: The speech was designed to reassure Democrats who say Biden has failed to deliver on a promise to make voting rights a central theme of his presidency.
sentences.zh: 这场演讲旨在安抚民主党人，此前他们指出拜登未能兑现将投票权作为其总统任期核心议题的承诺。

sentences.en: And it comes as Republican lawmakers in Texas try to adopt voting restrictions over the objections of their Democratic colleagues, many of whom have
sentences.zh: 在此之前，得克萨斯州的共和党议员试图不顾民主党同僚的反对通过投票限制法案，其中许多民主党人

sentences.en: fled the state to block the legislation.
sentences.zh: 已经逃离该州以阻挠这项立法。

sentences.en: We'll be asking my Republican friends in Congress and states and cities and counties to stand up for
sentences.zh: 我们将要求我在国会、各州、各市以及各县的共和党朋友们挺身而出，

sentences.en: God's sake and help prevent this concerted effort to undermine our election and the sacred right to vote.
sentences.zh: 看在上帝的份上，帮助阻止这场蓄意破坏我们选举和神圣投票权的行动。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Annie Brown, Jessica Chung, Rochelle Bonja,
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由安妮·布朗、杰西卡·钟、罗谢尔·邦贾、

sentences.en: Asta Chaturvedi, and Austin Mitchell.
sentences.zh: 阿斯塔·查图维迪和奥斯汀·米切尔制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Liz O.
sentences.zh: 由莉兹·奥·

sentences.en: Balin and Paige Cowett, contains original music by Dan Powell, and was engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 巴林和佩奇·考维特编辑，包含丹·鲍威尔的原创音乐，由克里斯·伍德担任音频工程。

sentences.en: Special thanks to Sean Hubler.
sentences.zh: 特别感谢肖恩·胡布勒。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》中，我们将为节日期间的招待做好准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人们宾至如归的妙招。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们对光线敏感吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they black out to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是不是喝断片了才睡觉。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们需要什么样的光线环境？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这非常具体。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有对什么过敏吗，对食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们习惯喝咖啡还是茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.zh: 在《纽约时报》应用程序或你喜欢的任何播客平台上搜索《Wirecutter秀》。
